questions.stem: A `Session` class has a `final String userId` and a plain `long expiresAtMillis`, both set in its constructor, which hands `this` to nobody. A login thread builds a session and stores it in a plain, non-volatile field. A request thread on another core later reads that field and gets the new reference. Which fields will it read as the constructor set them, on any JVM and any CPU?

options.text: Both fields, since the final and the plain one were set before the login thread stored the reference
options.says: the login thread's order of writes binds no other thread without an edge; the reader may get the reference without the plain field's value

options.text: Only userId, since a final field is frozen when the constructor ends and a racy read still sees it frozen
options.says: JLS 17.5 guarantees final fields to any thread that sees the reference after the constructor finished, even through a data race; plain fields get no guarantee

options.text: Both fields, since a reference is written atomically, so the object behind it arrives complete
options.says: atomicity of the reference write (JLS 17.7) means no half reference; it says nothing about the object's fields

options.text: Only expiresAtMillis, since a long is written in one step while a final reference can be read before its target
options.says: a long written in the constructor gets no guarantee through a race; the final reference field is the one JLS 17.5 covers

origin.section: final Fields Are Guaranteed Through a Race, and Nothing Else in the Object Is

questions.stem: A `Signing` class declares `static final KeyPair KEYS = Vault.fetchKeys();`. At startup the vault is restarting, so the first call to `Signing.sign(...)` fails with an exception from `fetchKeys()`. Thirty seconds later the vault is back, and requests keep calling `Signing.sign(...)`. What do those calls get until the process restarts?

options.text: Working signatures, since the next use of the class runs its initializer again and now reaches the vault
options.says: a class whose initializer threw is marked as failed and is never initialized again in that class loader

options.text: An ExceptionInInitializerError on every call, since the class keeps the first failure and throws it to each caller
options.says: only the first use gets ExceptionInInitializerError; later uses get NoClassDefFoundError

options.text: A NoClassDefFoundError on every call, since the class was marked as failed when its initializer threw
options.says: JLS 12.4.2 marks the class erroneous; every later use gets NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class

options.text: Working signatures, since the JVM retries a failed initializer once the first exception has been reported
options.says: nothing retries a failed initializer; only a new class loader or a restart initializes the class again

origin.section: A Static Initializer Publishes to Every Thread, and Fails for Every Thread

questions.stem: A loader thread constructs a `Tariff` whose fields are all plain (not final, not volatile), sets two more of its fields through setters, then calls `tariffs.put("2025-Q3", tariff)` on a `ConcurrentHashMap`. Nobody changes the tariff after that. A pricing thread later calls `tariffs.get("2025-Q3")` and gets it. What may the pricing thread read from the tariff's fields?

options.text: Every value written before the put, since the put happens-before the get that returned the tariff
options.says: a concurrent collection is a safe publication: everything written before the put is visible after the get that returns the element

options.text: Only the values written in the constructor, since the put publishes the tariff as its constructor left it
options.says: the edge covers every write made before the release, setters included; only changes after the put need an edge of their own

options.text: Possibly defaults for all of them, since the get makes the reference visible but not the fields behind it
options.says: the map's put/get edge orders all of the loader's earlier writes before the pricing thread's later reads

options.text: Possibly defaults for all of them, since only final fields reach a thread that did not build the tariff
options.says: an effectively immutable object needs one safe publication, not final fields; the final-field guarantee matters only for a racy reference

origin.section: Safe Publication Is an Edge From the Object's Construction to the Read of Its Reference

questions.stem: An `OrderBatcher` constructor runs `this.flusher = new Thread(this::flushLoop); flusher.start(); this.maxBatch = config.maxBatch();`, where `maxBatch` is a `final int`. `flushLoop` reads `maxBatch` as soon as it runs. What may `flushLoop` read?

options.text: The configured size, since maxBatch is final, and a final value is frozen before flushLoop can read it
options.says: the final-field guarantee is only for threads that see the object after its constructor finished; the flusher got it before

options.text: Possibly 0, since flusher.start() ran before maxBatch was set, and start() publishes only the Thread's own state
options.says: start() publishes every write the starting thread made before it, not only the Thread object's; the assignment after start() is what nothing orders

options.text: The configured size, since flusher.start() ran before flushLoop, and start() publishes the constructor's writes
options.says: the start() edge covers the writes before start(), not the assignment that comes after it

options.text: Possibly 0, since flusher.start() ran before maxBatch was set, and start() publishes only earlier writes
options.says: this escaped to the flusher before the constructor finished, so neither the start() edge nor the final-field guarantee covers maxBatch

origin.section: A Constructor That Lets this Escape Hands Out an Object Before It Is Built
